questions.question: 1. Which among the following represents a stack?

answers.a: People waiting at a counter, where the first person served is the first person who arrived
answers.b: A hand of bangles where pushing is wearing a new bangle
answers.c: A pile of plates at a dinner party

explanations.a: Incorrect. This situation follows an arrival-based service order rather than removal from the most recently added position.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Although bangles can be added and removed from one side, this is a less direct analogy for the standard stack model.
explanations.c: Correct. A pile of plates follows LIFO behavior because the most recently placed plate is normally removed first.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Movement around a merry-go-round does not represent insertion and removal from a single accessible end.

questions.question: 2. What is the time complexity of a push operation in a stack? What is the time complexity of a pop operation in a stack?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Standard stack push and pop do not require traversal through all stack elements.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A standard pop operation does not require processing every element in the stack.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A standard push operation does not require shifting or traversing all existing elements.
explanations.d: Correct. In a standard stack implementation, push and pop operate at the top and each takes constant time.

questions.question: 3. Consider these operations on an empty stack: push(3), push(5), pop(), push(10), push(11), pop(), push(100). What will be the stack configuration? The first number is the top of the stack and the last number is the bottom.

explanations.a: Correct. The first pop removes 5, the second pop removes 11, and push(100) places 100 above 10 and 3.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This sequence still contains elements that were removed by the pop operations.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This configuration omits the element 10 that remains in the stack after the second pop.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The element 11 is removed by the second pop operation and therefore does not remain in the stack.

questions.question: 4. If a stack is initially empty and the operations push(4), push(7), push(9), pop(), push(12) are performed, which element is at the top?

explanations.a: Incorrect. This element was inserted first and remains below the later elements.
explanations.b: Incorrect. This element remains in the stack but is not the most recently inserted element.
explanations.c: Incorrect. This element is removed by the pop operation.
explanations.d: Correct. The pop removes 9, after which push(12) places 12 at the top.

questions.question: 5. Which operation allows the top element of a stack to be inspected without removing it?

explanations.a: Correct. Peek, also called top in some implementations, reads the top element without deleting it.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Push inserts a new element into the stack rather than merely inspecting the top.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Pop removes the top element from the stack.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Enqueue is an insertion operation associated with queues.

questions.question: 6. What condition occurs when a pop operation is attempted on an empty stack?

explanations.a: Incorrect. Overflow is associated with attempting to add beyond the available capacity in a bounded stack.
explanations.b: Correct. Stack underflow occurs when a removal operation is attempted while the stack contains no elements.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Collision is primarily associated with situations such as hashing when multiple keys map to the same location.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Traversal refers to visiting elements or nodes and is not the error condition for removing from an empty stack.

questions.question: 7. A stack is used to evaluate a postfix expression. Which property of the stack makes it suitable for this task?

answers.a: It processes elements according to FIFO order
answers.b: It always stores elements in sorted order
answers.c: It provides LIFO access to operands and intermediate results
answers.d: It allows insertion only at the rear

explanations.a: Incorrect. FIFO ordering is the access discipline of a queue rather than a stack.
explanations.b: Incorrect. A stack does not automatically maintain its elements in sorted order.
explanations.c: Correct. LIFO access allows the most recently available operand or intermediate result to be retrieved during postfix evaluation.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Rear-based insertion is a characteristic used when describing queue operations.

questions.question: 8. A stack is implemented using an array of capacity 5. If the stack already contains 5 elements, what happens when another push operation is attempted?

answers.c: The oldest element is automatically removed
answers.d: The new element is inserted below the bottom element

explanations.a: Correct. In a fixed-capacity array implementation, attempting to push when all available positions are occupied results in overflow.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Underflow concerns attempting to remove an element when no element is available.
explanations.c: Incorrect. A standard fixed-capacity stack does not automatically discard the oldest element during push.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A stack does not provide an insertion position below its bottom element.

questions.question: 9. Which sequence of operations on an empty stack results in 20 being at the top while 10 remains below it?

explanations.a: Incorrect. The second push places 10 above the previously inserted element.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The pop removes the only element before 20 is inserted, leaving no 10 below it.
explanations.c: Correct. push(10) places 10 in the stack first, and push(20) places 20 above it.
explanations.d: Incorrect. The pop removes 20 before 10 is inserted, so the resulting stack has a different arrangement.
